description: REQ-A3 OAuth URL handling: spec extracts a URL via 'regex' from pane text and posts it through escalate.sh → Telegram for Dais to one-tap-click. Three security gaps: (1) the regex is unspecified — no anchoring requirement, no host whitelist (must be exactly https://claude.com/cai/oauth/authorize…); (2) if the pane has been polluted (anything that wrote to the terminal: an earlier tool output, a malicious shared lesson surfaced via cross-learn, a crafted gh issue body) a phishing URL like https://claude.com.evil.tld/... or a homograph could be extracted and forwarded; (3) Dais's threat model is 'one-tap click' so this is a high-value phishing target. PROP-A3 only asserts 'OAuth URL regex extracts a non-empty https URL when present' — non-empty https is not a security property. Combined with REQ-F1 Telegram POST having NO authentication / endpoint configuration spec, the attacker-controlled URL travels through an unauthenticated channel to a one-tap user.

evidence.snippet: (c) capture pane and extract the OAuth `https://claude.com/cai/oauth/authorize…` URL via regex, (d) call `escalate.sh <slot> needs-login <url>` so the URL surfaces to Dais's Telegram via the watcher cron
